concepts.name: Architecture perspective
concepts.description: A cross-cutting set of activities and checks applied across views to address a quality concern.

concepts.name: Security perspective
concepts.description: A perspective focused on protecting assets, reducing threats, and preserving security properties across the architecture.

concepts.name: Security property
concepts.description: A desired protection quality such as confidentiality, integrity, availability, accountability, or non-repudiation.

concepts.name: Attack surface
concepts.description: The set of entry points and exposed interactions through which an attacker might affect the system.

concepts.name: Security asset
concepts.description: A data item, capability, service, credential, or business function that requires protection.

concepts.name: Threat
concepts.description: A potential cause of harm to a security asset or security property.

concepts.name: Security control
concepts.description: A mechanism or process that reduces the likelihood or impact of a security threat.

concepts.name: Least privilege
concepts.description: The design principle that actors and components receive only the permissions required for their responsibilities.

concepts.name: Tenant isolation
concepts.description: The architectural separation of data, execution, configuration, or access between customers or organizational tenants.

concepts.name: Encryption boundary
concepts.description: The point at which data is protected or exposed as it moves or is stored in the system.

concepts.name: Audit trail
concepts.description: A record of security-relevant actions used for accountability, investigation, and compliance.

concepts.name: Secrets management
concepts.description: The controlled storage, rotation, access, and use of credentials, keys, and sensitive configuration.
